tasks.statement:
An identifier can arrive as a number or as a string. The enum Id { Num(u64), Text(String) } without a tag accepts both. Print the result of parsing the values 42, "abc", "7", and the result of parsing true (an error, printed as the word "error").

tasks.title: Trimming strings while parsing
tasks.statement:
The text field of the struct Say must be trimmed of surrounding whitespace already while parsing the JSON. Write a function trimmed(deserializer) and attach it with deserialize_with. Print the result of parsing the string {"text":"   hello  "} in Debug form.

Expected output:
`Say { text: "hello" }`
tasks.hint: fn trimmed<'de, D: Deserializer<'de>>(d: D) -> Result<String, D::Error> { let s = String::deserialize(d)?; Ok(s.trim().to_string()) }

tasks.title: Username as a type
tasks.statement:
The type Username (3 to 16 characters, only Latin letters and digits) is created by the function Username::parse(&str) -> Result<Username, String> (the error is the reason text: "short" for too short, "long" for too long, or "invalid character" for an invalid character). Attach parsing from JSON with #[serde(try_from = "String")]. Print the result of parsing the strings "anna", "ab", "a_very_long_username_here", "a b".

Expected output:
```
"anna": Ok(Username("anna"))
"ab": Err("short")
"a_very_long_username_here": Err("long")
"a b": Err("invalid character")
true
true
```
tasks.hint: impl TryFrom<String> for Username { type Error = String; ... }: serde calls it while parsing.

tasks.title: Application errors: status and code
tasks.statement:
The starter contains the enum AppError. Implement the methods status() -> StatusCode (NotFound → 404, Conflict → 409, Invalid → 422, Unauthorized → 401, Internal → 500) and code() -> &'static str ("not_found", "conflict", "invalid", "unauthorized", "internal"). main prints the pairs for all variants.

Expected output:
404 not_found
409 conflict
422 invalid
401 unauthorized
500 internal

tasks.title: AppError as a response
The ? operator and From
tasks.statement:
Implement From<std::num::ParseIntError> for AppError (the Invalid variant with a single text) and a handler GET /double/{n} with Path<String>: it parses n as i64 with the ? operator and responds with the doubled number; invalid text gives 422 with the body "invalid: not a number". The starter contains AppError with IntoResponse (Invalid(String)).

Expected output:
```
(200, "42")
(200, "-8")
(422, "invalid: not a number")
```
tasks.hint: impl From<ParseIntError> for AppError { fn from(_: ParseIntError) -> Self { AppError::Invalid(..) } }.

tasks.title: A custom ApiJson extractor
tasks.statement:
The starter contains AppError (BadRequest(String) → 400 code bad_request, Unsupported → 415 code unsupported, Invalid(String) → 422 code invalid; IntoResponse produces {"error":{"code":..,"message":..}}). Implement the extractor ApiJson<T>: a FromRequest that calls Json<T> and turns JsonRejection into AppError by the rejection's status (400, 415, otherwise 422), with the message rejection.body_text(). The handler POST /n takes ApiJson<Num> with the field n: i64 and responds with the number. Check a correct body, non-JSON, a wrong type, and a request without a content-type header.

Expected output:
200 5
400 bad_request
422 invalid
415 unsupported
tasks.hint: impl<S, T> FromRequest<S> for ApiJson<T> where T: DeserializeOwned, S: Send + Sync { type Rejection = AppError; async fn from_request(req: Request<Body>, state: &S) -> Result<Self, AppError> { ... } }

tasks.title: 404 and 405 in JSON format
tasks.statement:
A router with the route GET /ping ("pong") must answer unknown paths with 404 and the body {"error":{"code":"not_found"}}, and a wrong method with 405 and the body {"error":{"code":"method_not_allowed"}}. Use .fallback(..) and .method_not_allowed_fallback(..). Print the responses to GET /ping, GET /x, POST /ping.

Expected output:
(200, "pong")
(404, "{\"error\":{\"code\":\"not_found\"}}")
(405, "{\"error\":{\"code\":\"method_not_allowed\"}}")

tasks.title: Internal details go to the log
tasks.statement:
The handler GET /boom fails with the error Internal("sql: syntax error near 'FORM' at db.rs:12"). The client must get 500 and the body "internal error", while the details must go to the log (an Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>> from the state). Write the handler so that it records the detail in the log itself and returns the general error; main prints the response to the client and the log.

Expected output:
```
(500, "internal error")
["sql: syntax error near 'FORM' at db.rs:12"]
```
tasks.hint: Record the detail in the log before returning (StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, "internal error").

tasks.title: Request, row, and response
tasks.statement:
There are three types: CreateRoom { name } (the request), RoomRow { id, name, secret_key } (the database row), RoomOut { id, name } (the response). Implement From<RoomRow> for RoomOut and the handler POST /rooms: it parses CreateRoom, "saves" a row (id = the number of characters in the name, secret_key = "k-" + the name), and responds with RoomOut as JSON with status 201. The secret key must not appear in the response.

Expected output:
``(201, "{\"id\":5,\"name\":\"general\"}")``

tasks.title: A chain of error causes
tasks.statement:
Implement a chain of causes for AppError (Display and std::error::Error): AppError::Db(DbError), where source() returns the inner error; AppError::NotFound has no cause. Display: "database unavailable" for Db and "not found" for NotFound. DbError implements Display ("connection broken") and Error. The function chain(&dyn Error) -> Vec<String> collects the texts of the whole chain from the outer error to the deepest one.

Expected output:
```
["database unavailable", "connection broken"]
["not found"]
```
tasks.hint: fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn Error + 'static)>; loop: while let Some(e) = cur { ...; cur = e.source(); }

tasks.title: A cursor in the query string
tasks.statement:
GET /msgs?cursor=c123 accepts an optional cursor of the form "c" + a number. The type Cursor(u64) is parsed from a string through #[serde(try_from = "String")] (the error: "invalid cursor"). The handler responds "after N" (or "from start" if there is no cursor). For an invalid cursor axum returns 400. Print the responses for /msgs, /msgs?cursor=c42, /msgs?cursor=x1, and /msgs?cursor=c.

Expected output:
```
/msgs -> 200 from start
/msgs?cursor=c42 -> 200 after 42
/msgs?cursor=x1 -> 400
/msgs?cursor=c -> 400
```
tasks.hint: impl TryFrom<String> for Cursor: strip_prefix('c') and parse::<u64>().
